item.title: Ramla Bay Resort to give TCN workers €400 permit-renewal contribution
item.description: Ramla Bay Resort in Mellieħa has announced a contribution of up to €400 for each of its third-country national workers when their work permits are renewed, to help cover the extra costs of this year's Budget measures. The resort is also launching a company-wide service bonus and a new employee social and wellbeing fund fully funded by the company. It said it will support training for colleagues attending Maltese language courses and taking part in the I Belong programme, aimed at helping them integrate further into Maltese society.

Sources: Lovin Malta

item.title: Cleaner avoids jail for theft after original prison sentence quashed
item.description: A cleaner who was sentenced to three years in prison for stealing jewellery from two homes has been conditionally discharged after her original sentence was quashed. Magistrate Astrid May Grima said Seliam Ann Elbueshi Perry, 46, had served enough time since the offences, had stable employment and had returned some of the stolen jewellery. The case dates back to 2018, with thefts from flats in Sliema and Msida between 2017 and 2018, for which she pleaded guilty in December 2018.

item.title: Credit agency holds Malta's A2 rating but warns on spending and rule of law
item.description: Credit rating agency Moody's affirmed Malta's A2 rating with a stable outlook, but warned that continued government spending and institutional shortcomings are holding back an otherwise resilient economy. The agency expects the fiscal deficit to widen from 2.1% of GDP in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026 before easing to 2.7% in 2027, citing energy subsidies costing around €400 million, higher social security spending and growing public investment. It again flagged rule of law, corruption and money laundering supervision concerns, while noting that Budget 2027's higher tourist contributions and work permit fees could partly offset the additional spending.

item.title: BOV chair says employers should shoulder the cost of TCN budget measures
item.description: Bank of Valletta board chairperson Gordon Cordina said employers should bear the cost of the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals without long-term residency. Speaking on Campus 103.7, Cordina argued Malta needs an enterprising economy able to sustain the cost of attracting skilled workers rather than one built on low cost, and said employers would pass that expense on to consumers where necessary. Under the measures, affected workers lose free childcare and public transport, face a €996 annual charge to drive their own vehicles and a €400 fee when renewing their work permits.

item.title: Saint James performs first specialised heart procedures in private healthcare
item.description: Three patients have undergone specialised heart procedures at Saint James Hospital in Żejtun, marking the first time such interventions have been carried out in Malta's private healthcare sector. The work took place in the hospital's new €2.5 million Prof. Albert Fenech Cardiac Suite and included a coronary angiogram and a patent foramen ovale closure, a procedure that seals a small opening between the heart's upper chambers. Saint James says it is the only private hospital in Malta with a cardiac catheterisation laboratory, so patients needing such treatment no longer have to rely on the public health service or travel abroad.

item.title: Two injured after car overturns at Ħ'Attard roundabout
item.description: Two people were taken to Mater Dei Hospital after a serious accident at the roundabout near Monte Karmeli in Ħ'Attard, where a car overturned onto its side. Police said the incident happened at about 5am near a petrol station forecourt, when the driver, a 27-year-old man from Ħal Qormi, lost control of the vehicle; an 18-year-old passenger from Swieqi was also in the car. The driver suffered serious injuries and the passenger lighter ones, and police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Emeritus judge finds no basis for University probe into statistician Vince Marmarà
item.description: Statistician Vince Marmarà published the full conclusions of a report by retired judge Geoffrey Valenzia, who found no factual basis to justify a University of Malta investigation into alleged professional ethics breaches. Valenzia said the accusations levelled against Marmarà by Arnold Cassola were not supported by facts or evidence, and criticised them as serious and offensive personal allegations. Marmarà said he was making the conclusions public after the competent authorities confirmed that no laws had been breached in the professional work carried out by his company.

item.title: Malta and Turkey discuss closer cooperation on healthcare
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg held talks with Turkish counterpart Kemal Memişoğlu in Istanbul on closer cooperation in digital health, medical innovation and hospital infrastructure. The meetings took place on the sidelines of the 12th Turkish Medical World Congress and follow a two-day visit to Malta last week by a Turkish delegation led by Deputy Health Minister Şuayip Birinci, which toured Gozo General Hospital. Borg said the discussions came as Malta prepares major healthcare infrastructure investment, including an expansion of Mater Dei Hospital's emergency department and stronger digital healthcare systems.

item.title: Caritas warns Budget measures on migrants risk fuelling discrimination
item.description: Caritas Malta welcomed Budget 2027's social measures, including higher pensions and the minimum wage, extra support for people with disabilities and families in need, and government coverage of social security contributions for young people in long-term rehabilitation. The charity warned that the new fees targeting third-country nationals risk creating a divide between people seen as entitled to social protection and migrant workers treated primarily as economic units. Under the budget, workers without long-term residency lose free childcare and public transport, face a €996 annual charge to drive and a €400 infrastructure contribution fee, and pay higher work permit fees, though nurses and carers are exempt from the permit fee increase.

item.title: Court orders immediate release of tourist jailed over airport bomb remark
item.description: Magistrate Marse-Ann Farrugia ordered the immediate release of Croatian national Blazenko Djuran, 61, after finding that his continued detention was unlawful, upholding a habeas corpus application on his behalf. The court found that a language misunderstanding over the English word "charges" had resulted in his guilty plea being recorded as not guilty, when he had always insisted on his guilt. Djuran had been remanded since 23 October after a sarcastic remark to Ryanair staff at Malta International Airport that his hand luggage was not as though it contained a bomb. The detention was declared unlawful under Article 412B of the Criminal Code.

item.title: Momentum publishes the 22-question survey commissioned for the Yorgen Fenech case
item.description: Momentum published on Saturday the 22-question draft questionnaire that pollster Vincent Marmarà's company, Sagalytics, was commissioned to run for Raymond Fenech, uncle of businessman Yorgen Fenech, together with an extract from the terms of engagement. Respondents were asked whether they believed Fenech ordered the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia, whether the police investigation was fair, and whether their political beliefs would interfere with their objectivity as a juror. Marmarà confirmed to Times of Malta that the sample questionnaire was accurate, and the contract was signed on 2 July 2021. The disclosure follows Fenech's acquittal of involvement in Caruana Galizia's murder by an 8-1 jury verdict in September.

item.title: Għarb nursing home on agricultural land set for approval after 850 objections
item.description: A nursing home planned on agricultural land in Għarb is expected to be approved on 10 November after a fourth attempt, having attracted more than 850 objections. The Environment and Resources Authority deemed the application acceptable after the plans were scaled back from 94 beds to 48, though it said any intervention beyond the development zone remained unacceptable. Earlier applications for a nursing home on the same site were made in 1994, 2008 and 2022, and the latest proposal limits vehicle access to the ODZ to parking under the project site.

item.title: Qrendi residents gatecrash garden inauguration over major development
item.description: Residents and activists gatecrashed the inauguration of a new garden in Qrendi to confront Environment Minister Miriam Dalli over a proposed major residential development in the village. The dispute centres on planning application PC/00053/26, which proposes residential buildings reaching 17.5 metres high on vacant land off Triq Dun Nerik Mahoney and Triq San Nikola, close to a historic tower and a protected garden. Residents said they had lost confidence in the planning system and warned the scheme would permanently alter the village's skyline and consume one of its last open areas. Dalli acknowledged concerns about overdevelopment in rural villages but said she cannot intervene in Planning Authority decisions.
